guideTitle: The Best KVM Docking Stations for Sharing a Desk Between Two Computers
breadcrumbLabel: Best KVM Docking Stations for Two Computers
metaTitle: Best KVM Docking Stations for Two Computers (2026)
metaDescription: A KVM dock lets two computers share monitors, keyboard and mouse. We compared five KVM docks on host types, monitors, charging and refresh rate, plus three non-KVM alternatives.
introParagraphs: A KVM docking station lets two computers, such as a work laptop and a personal machine, share the same monitors, keyboard, mouse and often Ethernet, switching between them with a button. The key questions are what kind of computers you're connecting, how many monitors, and whether the dock charges laptops.

The AV Access docks charge two laptops over USB-C (60W or 100W each); the AV Access 8K and the 13-in-1 dock also accept desktops; the UGREEN shares three monitors but doesn't list laptop charging. Three non-KVM docks are included as the alternative of pairing a single-computer dock with a separate switch.
Our comparison is based on published specifications, not hands-on testing.

av-access-kvm-2monitor-mst.badge: Best for Two Laptops with Fast Monitors
av-access-kvm-2monitor-mst.summary: An AV Access KVM dock for two laptops and two monitors, with 60W to each PC and up to 2K 144Hz or 1080p 240Hz.
av-access-kvm-2monitor-mst.description:
This AV Access dock connects two laptops over USB-C and shares two monitors, keyboard, mouse and Ethernet between them, charging each at 60W. EDID emulation is intended to keep window positions and display settings stable when you switch.

It lists high-refresh support, up to 2K at 144Hz or 1080p at 240Hz, as well as 4K. 60W may be low for larger laptops.
av-access-kvm-2monitor-mst.skipIf: Your laptops need more power; the 100W AV Access model supplies it.

av-access-kvm-2monitor-100w.summary: An AV Access KVM dock with 100W to each of two laptops and dual 4K monitors.
av-access-kvm-2monitor-100w.description:
This AV Access model raises charging to 100W for each connected laptop, useful for larger machines, and supports two 4K monitors, 1G Ethernet and EDID emulation.

It cost less than the 60W MST model at the time of writing, though it doesn't list the same high-refresh modes.
av-access-kvm-2monitor-100w.bestFor: Two power-hungry laptops on one desk.
av-access-kvm-2monitor-100w.skipIf: You need a desktop connected; the AV Access 8K model supports desktops.

av-access-8k-kvm-gbe.badge: Best for Laptop and Desktop Mixes
av-access-8k-kvm-gbe.summary: An AV Access KVM for two computers, laptops or desktops, with up to 8K output and Gigabit Ethernet.
av-access-8k-kvm-gbe.description:
This AV Access model works with laptop and desktop combinations, which suits a personal desktop alongside a work laptop, with support up to 8K resolution, two monitors and Gigabit Ethernet.

It was the most expensive dedicated KVM here at the time of writing, and the listing summary doesn't give charging figures.
av-access-8k-kvm-gbe.bestFor: A desktop and a laptop sharing one set of monitors.
av-access-8k-kvm-gbe.skipIf: Both hosts are laptops; the 100W AV Access costs less.

kvm-2monitor-13in1-aluminum.summary: A 13-in-1 aluminum KVM dock with USB-C and HDMI/DisplayPort inputs, 100W and dual 4K up to 120Hz.
kvm-2monitor-13in1-aluminum.description:
This 13-in-1 KVM dock accepts USB-C or HDMI/DisplayPort inputs, charges at 100W and drives two monitors at 4K 60Hz or up to 4K 120Hz, in an aluminum case with the widest port selection among the KVMs here.

The brand isn't named in the listing.
kvm-2monitor-13in1-aluminum.bestFor: Two computers with lots of peripherals.
kvm-2monitor-13in1-aluminum.skipIf: You need three monitors; the UGREEN supports three.

ugreen-kvm-triple-monitor.summary: UGREEN's KVM for two computers and three monitors, up to 8K@60Hz or 4K@240Hz, cables included.
ugreen-kvm-triple-monitor.description:
The UGREEN is the lowest-priced option here and supports three monitors shared between two computers, with up to 8K at 60Hz or 4K at 240Hz, four USB 3.0 ports and an aluminum case.

It includes four DisplayPort and two HDMI cables, a power adapter and a controller. It's a KVM switch rather than a charging dock, so laptops need their own power.
specs: Included: 4 DP + 2 HDMI cables, adapter, controller
cons: Needs video cables from each computer
ugreen-kvm-triple-monitor.skipIf: You want single-cable laptop docking; the AV Access models charge laptops.

anker-prime-docking-14port.summary: A 14-port dock with 160W total output, dual 4K, 10Gbps data, Ethernet and audio; not Thunderbolt certified.
anker-prime-docking-14port.description:
This is a single-computer dock, not a KVM switch; it's included as the alternative of pairing a full dock with a separate KVM switch.

The Anker Prime 14-port works from a Thunderbolt 4 port but isn't Thunderbolt certified. It offers 14 ports, 160W total output shared across devices, dual 4K, 10Gbps data, Ethernet and audio.

It costs less than the certified docks at the time of writing. It lacks certified Thunderbolt bandwidth and daisy-chaining.
cons: Laptop charging limited by USB PD
anker-prime-docking-14port.bestFor: Many USB peripherals without Thunderbolt devices.
anker-prime-docking-14port.skipIf: You need to switch between two computers; any AV Access model does it in one box.

anker-prime-dl7400-displaylink.summary: A 14-port DisplayLink dock with triple 4K at 60Hz, 140W output and a cooling fan.
anker-prime-dl7400-displaylink.description:
This is a single-computer dock, not a KVM switch; it's included as the alternative of pairing a full dock with a separate KVM switch.

The Anker Prime DL7400 drives three 4K displays at 60Hz through DisplayLink, which is uncommon, with 140W total output, a built-in cooling fan and a display status indicator.

Anker lists it for Windows laptops with the latest DisplayLink driver installed. It isn't Thunderbolt certified.
anker-prime-dl7400-displaylink.skipIf: You need two-computer switching; a dedicated KVM dock handles it.

plugable-tb4-dock-tbt-udm.summary: A Thunderbolt 4 certified dock with 100W, dual 4K HDMI or single 6K, 6 USB, SD and Gigabit Ethernet.
plugable-tb4-dock-tbt-udm.description:
This is a single-computer dock, not a KVM switch; it's included as the alternative of pairing a full dock with a separate KVM switch.

The Plugable TBT-UDM is the straightforward certified Thunderbolt 4 choice: 100W charging, dual 4K over HDMI or a single 6K display, six USB ports, an SD reader and Gigabit Ethernet, driverless on macOS and Windows.

It has fewer display outputs than the Dell, and dual display depends on your laptop's support.
plugable-tb4-dock-tbt-udm.bestFor: Mac or Windows Thunderbolt laptops with two monitors.
plugable-tb4-dock-tbt-udm.skipIf: You need to share monitors between two computers; choose a KVM dock.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Two USB-C laptops, or a mix with a desktop that needs HDMI/DisplayPort inputs.
Most here share two; the UGREEN shares three.
60W or 100W per host on the AV Access docks; the UGREEN doesn't list charging.
High-refresh monitors need a KVM that lists those modes, like the AV Access MST model.

faq.q: What does a KVM dock do?
faq.a: It lets two computers share monitors, keyboard, mouse and other peripherals, switching with a button.
The AV Access models list 60W or 100W per laptop; check others.
The AV Access 8K and 13-in-1 list desktop support via HDMI/DisplayPort.
It keeps each computer seeing the monitors while switched away, which helps windows stay in place.
As an alternative: a full dock per computer plus a separate KVM switch.

bottomLine: For two laptops, the AV Access 100W model charges both at full USB-C power, and the MST model suits high-refresh monitors. For a laptop and desktop, the AV Access 8K or the 13-in-1 dock accepts both.
The UGREEN is the low-cost way to share three monitors, mainly between desktops. The Anker and Plugable docks are single-computer alternatives.
